claims.text: Combining high-throughput DSC, in situ high-temperature synchrotron XRD, and atomistic free-energy simulations can determine melting temperature accurately across a broad range of high-entropy alloys.
The integrated approach can accurately determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The integrated approach can accurately determine volume change at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The integrated method is more efficient than conventional single-composition analyses.
The target alloys are well-mixed, single-phase or limited-multiphase solid solutions with systematically varied compositions.
DSC heat-flow anomalies can identify the onset and thermal signature of melting.
XRD can identify alloy phase composition and crystal structure.
In situ high-temperature synchrotron XRD can track melting and phase transformations in real time.
Atomistic simulation with a validated interatomic potential can be applied to a high-entropy alloy.
Atomistic free-energy simulations can be calibrated to mirror experimental heating rates and compositional variations.
Matching composition and temperature control synchronizes DSC thermal events with XRD phase-change signatures.
DSC and XRD signatures can be incorporated directly into free-energy simulations to predict and refine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Cross-validation between experiment and simulation ensures reliable thermodynamic-property determination.
Melting temperatures and fusion thermodynamic quantities will typically be determined within a 5–10% error margin.
Traditional single-composition, ex situ DSC or XRD analyses generally have lower accuracy and more limited compositional applicability than the proposed method.
The method should perform well when oxidation is controllable and phase evolution is relatively simple.
Rapid oxidation, extreme inhomogeneity, and complex multiphase behavior outside the simulation calibration range may reduce accuracy.
Local microstructural inhomogeneity and minor oxide formation may impair DSC signal clarity and XRD resolution.
Systematic experiment–simulation discrepancies greater than approximately 15% across multiple compositions would falsify the integrated approach.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies inert atmospheres, whereas the conditions allow ambient or inert-gas environments while stating that these avoid oxidation; an ambient atmosphere does not generally provide the same oxidation control.
